questions.scenario: Two development teams at a company will build separate generative AI apps. The company wants one bill, one set of network and security settings, and a separate workspace for each team's model deployments and agents.
questions.question: What should you create?

options.text: One Foundry resource that contains two projects
options.why: Correct. The resource holds shared billing and security, and each project is a separate team workspace.

options.text: Two Foundry resources that each contain one project
options.why: Two resources would duplicate billing and security settings.

options.text: One project that contains two Foundry resources
options.why: Resources contain projects, not the other way round.

options.text: Two Azure subscriptions with one model deployment each
options.why: Separate subscriptions do not meet the single bill requirement and are not needed for workspace separation.

questions.explanation: A Foundry resource provides shared billing, networking and security. Projects inside the resource give each team its own deployments, agents, files and evaluations.

questions.question: A developer must be able to use model deployments and build agents in a Foundry project. The developer must not be able to manage the Foundry resource or assign roles. Which role should you assign?

options.why: Foundry Owner grants full access, which exceeds the requirement.
This role manages the resource, which the developer must not do.
Correct. Foundry User allows building and using resources in a project without management rights.
Reader allows viewing only and does not allow building agents or calling deployments.

questions.explanation: Foundry User, formerly Azure AI User, is the least-privilege role for developers who build in a project.

questions.question: Which TWO items are stored at the project level in Microsoft Foundry?

options.why: Correct. Agents are created and versioned inside a project.
Correct. Evaluation runs belong to a project.
Billing is associated with the Foundry resource, not individual projects.

options.text: The network isolation settings for the whole resource
options.why: Networking is configured on the Foundry resource.

questions.explanation: Projects are team workspaces that hold deployments in use, agents, files and evaluations. The parent resource holds billing, networking and security.

questions.question: Which name refers to the set of services formerly known as Azure AI services, such as Azure Speech, Azure Language and Azure Vision?

options.why: Foundry Models refers to the model catalog and deployments.
Correct. Azure Speech, Azure Language, Azure Vision and Content Understanding are Foundry Tools.
The Agent Service hosts agents. It is not the name for the former Azure AI services.
Guardrails are safety controls such as content filters.

questions.explanation: The services previously called Azure AI services are now Foundry Tools, for example Azure Speech in Foundry Tools.

questions.question: Which value should a client application use to connect to a specific Foundry project by using the Foundry SDK?

options.text: The project endpoint, in the format https://<resource-name>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project-name>
options.why: Correct. The project endpoint identifies both the resource and the project.
A subscription ID does not identify a project endpoint.

options.text: The name of the model in the model catalog
options.why: Catalog names identify models, not the project to connect to.
Resource group names are not used as connection endpoints.

questions.explanation: Applications connect to a project through its project endpoint, which is shown on the project overview page in the Foundry portal.
